text:
sara: Quick frag — ran a combined activation-aware quant (AWQ) + Smooth-style activation scaling on redwood-13b-32k variant for long-context (64k & 128k). Results look inconsistent: perplexity and SQuAD F1 dip at 64k, but 128k run is much closer to baseline. Sharing configs/logs below.

alex: can you paste the exact config? batch size / kv cache mode / act-scaling params?

sara: here is the config I used: 
```yaml
model: redwood-13b-32k
quant: mix_awq_smooth
bits: 8
act_scaling: per_channel
smooth_alpha: 0.65
kv_cache: sharded
batch_tokens: 64
max_ctx: 128000
```

davinder: what's the eval harness? prefix-only or sliding-window? which metrics?

sara: Eval suite: SQuADv2 (QA F1), perplexity on eval-lm-64k, and a small codegen hallucination smoke test. For 128k I used sliding-window with stride=4k, for 64k I ran prefix-only to mimic real prefix caching.

jordan: raw numbers:
- 64k: perplexity fp16 -> quant: 12.1 -> 13.9, SQuAD F1 87.6 -> 84.2 (regression ~3.4)
- 128k: perplexity 12.3 -> 12.6, SQuAD F1 87.4 -> 86.9 (minor)
- memory savings: 64k quant ~28% mem reduction; 128k ~32%

alex: interesting — regression only at 64k. maybe an activation-shift interaction with KV cache sharding / concatenation and chunk boundaries. Did you try single-shard (no sharding) vs sharded?

sara: tried single-shard (all kv on same GPU) — 64k regression still present. Bumped smooth_alpha to 0.75 and added per-layer activation clipping — got marginal improvement (~+0.6 F1).

davinder: can you dump per-layer activation scale stats? looking for outlier layers.

sara: sample medians from a profiling pass: 
layer_1: 0.92
layer_6: 1.45
layer_11: 2.8
layer_20: 0.98
layer_28: 3.6
layer_37: 0.45

sara: hypothesis: small quantization rounding errors for KV tensors accumulate when long prefixes are cached, and activation scaling mismatch across chunk concatenation amplifies the error.

jordan: did you try disabling KV prefix caching (i.e., recompute KV each request) as a binary test?

sara: yes — with prefix cache disabled the 64k regression disappears: SQuAD F1 moves to 86.8 (close to baseline). So caching appears to be the smoking gun.

alex: OK — two practical mitigations: 1) better per-block / concatenation-aware activation rescaling when writing/reading KV, 2) hybrid precision: keep keys/values in FP16 (or FP8) and quantize weights/activations. Try marking KV tensors as higher precision.

sara: ran a hybrid run (KV fp16, weights AWQ int8): 64k F1 improved to 87.2. Memory cost +12% vs pure int8 but still below full fp16. Good tradeoff for Dedicated deploys.

quant-bot: job 1765432310-compute-finish: AWQ+smooth_alpha=0.75 finished — SQuAD F1 86.9. Note: kv_fp16 hybrid run queued (job id 1765432350).

davinder: also try varying sliding stride for 128k to see if chunk boundary frequency matters. smaller stride -> less concatenation artifact?

sara: running stride sweep (2k/4k/8k): prelims show stride=2k reduces regression magnitude, stride=8k makes it worse. Suggests chunk boundary alignment is a factor.

alex: good. For rollout: we need a deployment profile for Dedicated and a fallback plan for Hosted. Add memory budgets and a canary rule.

sara: deployment snippet I will use: 
```json
{
  "deployment": "dedicated-13b-awq-hybrid",
  "gpu_mem_limit": "48GB",
  "kv_policy": "fp16-for-kv, int8-for-weights",
  "fallback": "on-failure -> fp16-variant",
  "batching": "continuous, max_tokens=64, latency_target=150ms"
}
```

jordan: add this model variant in Console as `unstable-longctx` and wire an eval-alert: if SQuAD F1 drops > 1.5 relative to baseline for 64k prefix runs, auto-rollback.

sara: will open a PR to add the variant, the evalsets, and the rollout policy. Thanks all :pray: I'll post the final artifact + perf logs when queued jobs finish.

alex: :eyes: please include the per-layer delta histogram and a small script to toggle KV precision in CI. That will help automation.

sara: noted — adding script and tests to the onboarding PR.
